chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: A man had the obligation of Hajj (ḥajjat al-Islām) upon him, and he intended to perform Hajj. He was told: 'Marry, then perform Hajj.' He said: 'If I marry before I perform Hajj, my slave will be free.' So he married before performing Hajj. The Imam said: 'His slave was emancipated.' I said: 'He did not intend the face of God by his emancipation.' He said: 'It is a vow in obedience to God, and Hajj is more deserving than marriage and more obligatory upon him than marriage.' I said: 'Indeed, Hajj is voluntary (taṭawwuʿ).' He said: 'And even if it is voluntary, it is an act of obedience to God, the Mighty and Majestic; he has emancipated his slave.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on emancipating a slave when a man marries before performing Hajj as part of a vow?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a vow to free a slave upon marrying before Hajj is binding because the act serves as obedience to God, regardless of whether the intention was purely for His sake or merely to fulfill the condition. The Imam emphasizes that Hajj holds precedence over marriage in this context, reinforcing the principle that voluntary acts of worship can carry the weight of obligatory obedience when linked to a vow. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that the validity of a nadhr relies on its alignment with divine command rather than the perfection of the vow-maker's internal intent.
